meta.note: Ubiquitous-language ontology for task-framework's domain: the vocabulary the code embodies, and the explicit typed relations between terms (is-a, part-of, relates, persists, references, describes). Deliberately separate from concept_store/concepts.json -- that store is architecture PER MODULE (one summary per file, enforced 1:1 by tests/test_concepts.py) and answers 'what does this module promise'. This file is vocabulary PER DOMAIN TERM and answers 'what is this thing, and what is it to the others' -- a term here can span several modules, and a module can define several terms, so it does not fit concept_store's per-file shape. Ground truth is still the code; this is a durable, human-readable map of the graph rather than N separate summaries.

bounded_contexts.Task Tracking: The core domain: tasks, epics, checklists, links between tasks, and which task is currently active.
bounded_contexts.Loop Memory: Lessons the grooming/introspection loop produces that nothing else can hold -- separate vocabulary, separate lifecycle, only loosely coupled to Task Tracking by citation.
bounded_contexts.Architectural Knowledge: What each source module promises, tracked in concept_store/concepts.json -- describes the codebase itself, not tasks or memories.

Task.definition: One unit of work: id, type, status, resolution (checklist), tags, notes, grooming findings, introspection reports. The single typed object the whole domain is built around.

Epic.definition: Not a distinct kind of thing -- a Task whose type field is 'epic', used to group other Tasks under it. There is no separate Epic class, table, or lifecycle.

ResolutionItem.definition: One checklist entry (text, done) inside a Task's resolution list. A Task's progress is derived by counting these, never stored as a separate counter.

Link.definition: A directed, typed connection between two Tasks (from_id, to_id, rel), rel drawn from the closed vocabulary TASK_EDGE_RELATIONS. Stored in task_edges, never inside a Task's own JSON blob.

TaskStore.definition: The Repository for Task: reads and writes tasks, edges, and commits. Deliberately does no rule-checking of its own -- validation lives entirely in taskfw/lifecycle.py.

ActiveTaskPointer.definition: Which task_id is currently 'active' for a scope. A single in-memory value, not persisted, not a stack -- gone on process restart. Not a field on Task itself.

MemoryRecord.definition: A lesson introspection produced: a constraint, technique, or recurring pitfall that nothing else in Task Tracking can hold. Has a derived 'standing' (confirmed/contradicted/disputed/superseded), computed fresh from its links on every read, never stored.

Concept.definition: A durable summary of what one source module promises and what must stay true of it -- description, contracts, invariants, evidence. Keyed by module path, enforced 1:1 against the real file tree by tests/test_concepts.py.

relations.subject: Epic
relations.note: type='epic' is a value on the same Task record, not a separate class or table -- there is no independent Epic to fall out of sync with Task.

relations.subject: ResolutionItem
relations.note: Nested inside task.resolution; no identity or lifecycle of its own outside the Task that holds it.

relations.subject: Link
relations.note: A task_edges row only exists in relation to two Tasks (from_id, to_id); it is never addressed by an id of its own, and removal (tasks__unlink) is deliberately ungated so a legacy rel can't get stuck.

relations.subject: TaskStore
relations.note: The Repository for the Task aggregate; persistence and validation stay separable because TaskStore enforces no rules itself.

relations.subject: ActiveTaskPointer
relations.note: Names the currently-active task_id per scope; ephemeral and non-persisted, never a property stored on Task.

relations.subject: MemoryRecord
relations.note: Cited to the task it was learned from (learned_from) -- a pointer INTO Task Tracking from a different bounded context, never reachable by walking Task's own fields.

relations.subject: Concept
relations.note: Keyed by module path, not by task_id -- Architectural Knowledge shares no term with Task Tracking or Loop Memory; the only connection between the three bounded contexts is this ontology file itself.
